speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the Strategy and Action Plan set out in the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Taskforce report (a) whether there will be resources provided for ground-up or grassroots efforts to support the action plans; and (b) how long will it take for Family Nexus centres which provide integrated health and social services for families with young children and couples planning for marriage and parenthood to be established at all polyclinics in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the setting up of Family Nexus sites under the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Taskforce’s Strategy and Action Plan (a) what is the timeline for rolling out this plan; and (b) when can residents of Woodgrove division expect to have access to such facilities at the Woodlands Polyclinic and other community spaces within Woodlands town.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister, I assume these are Question Nos 28 to 31 on the Order Paper?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in both the questions for oral and written answers by Dr Wan Rizal,1,2,3,4,5 which are scheduled for subsequent Sittings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If he agrees that the questions have been addressed, it may not be necessary for him to proceed with the questions for future Sittings, Sir.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the report, we set out action plans to help keep mothers and children healthy, tackling challenges such as the rising age of first-time mothers and incidence of childhood obesity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The various initiatives are designed to serve families better by wrapping both health and social services around them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about the progress and evaluation of various initiatives.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the 28 initiatives have only been rolled out over the last two years, we will evaluate them from 2025 onwards, based on their effectiveness in achieving their intended outcomes and other dimensions such as participation rate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In particular, Dr Wan Rizal asked about the reach of Project HOME, which stands for HOlistic Management and Enablement, and another project, HEADS-UPP or HEAlth and Development SUpport in Preschool Partnerships.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just to remind Members, these are pilots and therefore small cohorts are involved.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On how we are evaluating the key initiatives related to mental health screening and support for mothers, we will obtain feedback from participants and monitor the percentage of pregnant women identified and who have received appropriate follow-up care as well as improvement in their postpartum mental health.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Dr Wan also mentioned some areas for improvement, which the Taskforce had identified – rising age of mothers at childbirth, low birth weight and maternal mental health.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, we make more information available to all as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do this by increasing access so that everyone can self-help, by publishing guidelines and providing bite-sized information on Parent Hub and other websites.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The guidelines also help frontline providers in their work in supporting families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, we are introducing more accessible programmes, such as community antenatal education programmes at Choa Chu Kang by the National University Hospital System (NUHS) and at Family Nexus sites by healthcare clusters.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third, our public healthcare system proactively identifies those who are at-risk or need more help and offers additional support as needed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Across KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) and National University Hospital (NUH), all pregnant women will be screened for mental health conditions and those who need help will be provided follow-up care.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: KKH provides a Psychological Resilience in Antenatal Management (PRAM) programme to provide antenatal mental health screening, materials on mental health during obstetric visits and follow-ups with women at risk of developing postnatal depression.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NUH runs the ProPEL programme, which stands for Promoting Parental Emotional Health to Enhance Child Learning, and similarly identifies patients to ensure timely follow-up and care.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NUH has also extended their Women’s Emotional Health Service programme to women receiving care at NUH up to six years after their children are born, up from the follow-up period of one year previously, to ensure mothers receive adequate support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The programmes at KKH and NUH have benefited over 2,200 women.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Childhood obesity is a significant risk factor for developing obesity and other chronic illnesses later in life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Proper diet, sufficient physical activity and sleep, and balanced screen use can minimise sedentary lifestyles and reduce obesity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Multiple agencies across the health, education and social domains have worked together to introduce various measures to tackle childhood obesity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the area of nutrition, we put out a set of guidelines for feeding and eating in infants and young children in February 2024.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) is working with preschools and mainstream schools to provide healthier meals for students.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To ensure children have sufficient physical activity, preschools and schools are catering time for physical activities and raising awareness of the need to remain physically active.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government and schools cannot do this alone.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Behaviours still and will need to be sustained both in and out of school-time to be effective.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will continue to engage parents and encourage partners to improve access to healthier choice meals and physical activities in the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To help families better manage screen use and encourage balanced screen-time in children aged zero to 12, we issued the Guidance on Screen Use in Children in March 2023.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The advisory has been disseminated to medical associations, polyclinics, general practitioners (GPs) and preschools, and are available as resources on Parent Hub and Parents Gateway for parents of Ministry of Education (MOE) students.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some polyclinics have also incorporated screen use check-ins and education as part of child health visits.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The four Family Nexus pilot sites are actively engage parents on screen use habits of children.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the past months, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) have been discussing the need for more decisive and effective measures to shape the habits of device usage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MOH and MSF oversee the key touchpoints for children up to six years old through healthcare and preschools touchpoints.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will make our advice clearer and more definitive, deliver them consistently across all healthcare settings, with more reminders, put them into practice in preschools and find ways to encourage their adoption at home.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will share more about these efforts in coming months.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There has been positive ground feedback received on Family Nexus, from both partners and families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are tapping on these pilot sites to test out different models of bringing together partners to offer co-located programmes and services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MOH will study which elements of these models are most effective and explore how they can be scaled to residents in other regions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I mentioned Project HOME and HEADS-UPP earlier in my response.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MOH works closely with MSF, MOE and community partners to provide holistic health and social support through these two initiatives.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Social workers and preschool educators are equipped with skills to identify and refer preschool children who are at-risk of health, developmental, behavioural and dental issues to KKH for Project HOME or NUH for HEADS-UPP for further assessment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Home visits are made to families who have more complex needs to provide additional support to the parents and to enable fast-tracking of referrals for medical appointments as needed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To improve access, we have expanded community-based services to support children, adolescents and women in the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They can now access services such as antenatal classes, breastfeeding and lactation support and screening for maternal mental health at polyclinics and Family Nexus sites closer to homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our community nurses and other frontline colleagues play a key role in ensuring that services in the community are integrated and delivered well.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They support families and children with their specialised skills, such as growth and developmental assessment and counselling on common childhood illnesses and allergies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition, they help to link and direct families to other related services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will need to continue to count on them to care for families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about the challenges we face.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is still much to be done and many of these initiatives require close coordination among multiple partners and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also need to raise awareness of the importance of anchoring healthy behaviours as early in life as possible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I encourage everyone to share the report and resources such as Parent Hub more widely to families, during programmes and healthcare appointments, and via schools and Government platforms, so that more families can benefit and we can better help the next generation to grow well and realise their potential.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for a very comprehensive update of the work that the CAMH Taskforce has done.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But because several of the initiatives are now still in the pilot phase, can HPB, being a national agency, take on maybe baseline training where most of the community centres can offer this, so that we can cover as many of these mothers and children as we can?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I would say this is the first time we are actually trying to bring that many agencies across three domains: education, health and social support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Already, it is complicated because while everyone can do their work well, coordinating with one another in ensuring the support is done holistically is something we need to learn to do better.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I would say that at the initial stages, the referrals that are designed into the programmes are being done properly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, when a social service agency, for example, sees some health issues in the family, they do not just report; they make sure that it is addressed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If it is very complex, they ensure that the community nurses, for example, will attend to them and vice versa.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A health point like Family Nexus may find, during the interview, that they have other issues than just medical attention needed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That, too, has helped coordination among these agencies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Co-location is one solution so that when they come, they may be going for a particular issue to be addressed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But during the interview and triage, we also find out that there are other issues, and the agencies are already on hand and onsite to address the issues, if they want it to be done that way.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, I also see that sometimes the mother needs more help than the children they bring to the Nexus.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The children then get support and playing time, for example, while the issues of the mother are being addressed.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe that this is a wonderful initiative, something that we have been waiting for, for some time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I have a number of supplementary questions, Mr Speaker.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Is it okay if I go beyond the two?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Please ask all of them at one go and try to keep it succinct.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: What considerations would the Ministry take into account when wanting to expand to other regions?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I believe there are other regions which would also like to have these services.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: The second question is about the usage of screen time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: This is something that came up very strongly in the paper and there are only guidelines.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Are there plans for the Ministry to consider making it into legislation, where we can limit the usage of these devices for children?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Although we want to address obesity on its own, I remember back then that when we talked about obesity, a group of students in schools usually are sidelined.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: As we address this issue, I was wondering how we could better manage this situation so that we do not segregate this community too much where the children themselves are being targeted for being obese.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When we designed the four Family Nexus centres, we considered a few models to try out.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One model is like the one in our Tampines Hub, a community point where the community comes together naturally, regularly and makes a place where everyone is familiar with, but there are no medical facilities available, not like a polyclinic.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have another where it is actually a polyclinic and then we infused social services, so that if they come for medical attention, they can be referred to the social service agency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On screen time, it is a guideline right now.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the end of the day, to legislate something for the service providers is going to be really difficult because it is a complex issue involving both the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and MOH.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And everywhere in the world, we are trying to address this issue and looking for solutions to them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we can put this control in the hands of our parents to understand the different kinds of screen time that they are exposing their children to, especially when they are very young.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Growing Up in Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes (GUSTO), for example, talked about television (TV) time.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the very early years, a child may be watching TV, totally captured and enamoured by what is happening on TV, and we think, "Oh, the child is enjoying the show." But what GUSTO has found is that it is stimulating the brain with lights.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: All the child is looking at is light.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He does not understand what he is watching, and the stimulation on the brain is not good for the child.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, when we look at other kinds of screen use, we have to understand whether it is for interactive purposes, which is recommended, but still must be regulated for different age groups; whether it is passive, where the child is watching and nobody is interacting; or, even worse still, in the background; where nobody is watching but it is in the background.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, all these are kinds of screen device use which our parents must know about, more so because of social media and the ability of digital channels, like YouTube and so forth, so that we are aware about what we are exposing our children to and how their brains are developed and, in fact, even how their social behaviours are shaped.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They are very well thought out and easy to use.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do not need regulations to get these things understood.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do not need lawyers to understand what they are.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just read them and they are very easy to use.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Remember three things: need for interaction; avoid passive watching; and, worse still, do not have background screen use.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But a lot more effort ought to be done upstream.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: GUSTO studies also showed that there are things that we can do with our children that can prevent obesity setting in.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Just getting children to chew more while they are growing up and not swallowing everything does affect obesity rate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Instead of us always trying to address the issues when they are in primary and secondary school, growing obese, actually there are things that we can do to address these issues as they are growing up.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That is why Family Nexus, the polyclinics, the interventions we are making with our mothers as they give birth to their children, other than lactation and so forth, these are important ideas, concepts, findings that we hope can help our children grow and develop their potential as much as possible by addressing and helping them far up and downstream as much as possible.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for the insightful sharing.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The other supplementary question is in relation to the expansion of the Nexus centres, which the Minister had given an earlier response to my Parliamentary colleague Dr Wan Rizal's supplementary question, I have asked Parliamentary Questions on this as well, specifically in relation to whether these expansions will be rolled out in due course to our Marsiling-Yew Tee Group Representation Constituency's Woodgrove divisions, that will, of course, definitely benefit the residents of Woodgrove and also Marsiling.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The gist of why there is an emphasis for this is because we are expecting a lot of Build-To-Order (BTO) families with young children who will be moving in.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, I hope that the Ministry can, when it comes to expansion, take this into consideration when deciding on the locations for Nexus centres to be constructed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope that this can give the support to improve our TFR because this is part of the programmes that we want to put in place to help make Singapore that is "Made for Families", and to know that we will do everything and anything to support our mothers, particularly, in raising their children and having families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, it is already available to all OB/GYN specialists and hospitals, and I believe that within the fraternity, they are referring to this for their practice.
